reasoning_traces.think:
The trial-and-error framework models learning as a sequential decision process governed by stochastic action selection and reward feedback. Each trial generates an outcome that modifies subsequent action probabilities via Bayesian updating. In the context of the rat-in-maze paradigm, this translates to a Markovian transition system where states correspond to spatial positions and actions to directional movements. The fox terrier's gate-opening behavior illustrates how complex tasks decompose into elemental manipulations subject to trial refinement. These primitives form a dual structure: one layer representing the probabilistic evolution of behavioral policies, and another encoding the deterministic mechanics of environmental interaction. Failure modes arise when reward signals become decoupled from actions or when the agent lacks sufficient exploration capacity.
